variants.hypothesis: Density: the duration right after the label instead of pinned to the far right, so the eye does not travel 500px to read how long a call took.

verdicts.reasons: The only visible difference is where the duration goes: A puts it in a right-aligned column at about x=738, and B puts it in muted text right after the label. In the default and group stories at 1280px, A leaves a gap of roughly 500px between short labels like 'Ran pnpm test billing' and '6s', so the number floats apart from its row and pulls the eye to the right edge. B keeps it next to the label, which matches how T3's 'Worked for 3m 43s' reads and matches B's own collapsed 'Worked for 50s, 4 steps' summary. A's column fits Harbour's session list a little better, since that list right-aligns its time ('2d'), and it makes durations easy to scan down. In B the open-row chevron now sits alone at the far right, away from the label and duration (default 'Open', error and streaming stories), but that is a small cost. Error, streaming, long-content truncation (where both still fit '1m 14s' after the cut-off label) and the 420px mobile and group stories are otherwise the same and work well in both.

The two versions differ only in where the duration sits. A puts it in muted text right after the label ("Ran pnpm test billing 6s"), and B pushes it to a right-hand column next to the chevron. At 1280px, B's durations in the default and group stories sit about 500px away from labels like "Read src/billing/charge.ts". The rows have no background or divider to connect them, so it's hard to tell which time goes with which row and the list feels loose. A keeps each time attached to its row, which matches T3's inline "Worked for 3m 43s". B does line its durations up in a column, like the "2d" in Harbour's session list, which makes the times easy to scan and earns it a slightly higher consistency score. At 420px (mobile and group stories), B's column fits well and loses nothing, and so does A. Error, streaming, long-content, copy and the expanded panels are identical in both, so those scores are the same.

The only visible difference is where the duration sits. In A it is right-aligned at about x=738. In B it follows the label inline. At 1280px in A's default and group stories, short labels like 'Ran pnpm test billing' end about 550px before their '6s', so the eye has to cross empty space to connect the time to its call. B keeps 'Ran pnpm test billing 6s' and 'Running pnpm test 12s' together, which reads like T3's 'Worked for 3m 43s'. In B the open-row chevron sits alone at the far right (default 'Open', error, streaming), slightly less tidy than A's '6s ⌄' pair. A's right-hand time column matches how the Harbour session list right-aligns '2d' and status, so A scores a little higher on consistency. At 420px both work: A's column scans well and B's inline times stay next to their labels without wrapping. Error, streaming, long-content and copy are the same in both, apart from the duration placement.

variants.hypothesis: Hierarchy: the running call's label in the normal text colour, finished calls muted, so what the agent is doing now reads first.

verdicts.reasons: The only visible difference between the two is the running row's label. B shows 'Running pnpm test' (default Statuses, streaming, mobile-420) and 'Running pnpm test billing' (group Running, group-420) at full brightness, while A keeps them as muted as finished rows. In A, only the small sky spinner shows that a call is live, so in the Statuses list and the Running group the active call reads like a finished one. B's emphasis also matches Harbour's session list, where working sessions get bright titles and settled ones go quiet. One cost in B is that the running row and the failed 'Ran pnpm migrate --env staging' row now share the same brightness, so the error stands out a little less. Its red icon and red-bordered panel still set it apart. Everything else is identical in both: the error panel, long-content wrapping and scroll, the collapsed 'Worked for 50s, 4 steps' summary, the 420px layouts, and the spacing and copy. Those criteria get the same scores.

A and B differ in one place only: the label of the running row. A shows it in bright foreground; B leaves it the same muted grey as finished rows. In A's group 'Running' story and its streaming story, 'Running pnpm test billing' / 'Running pnpm test' is the first thing you see. In B the only cue is the small, thin sky spinner, so the live call blends in with 'Read src/billing/charge.ts' and 'Searched for retryCharge'. This is clearest on the 420px mobile shot, where B's 'Running pnpm test' looks almost identical to 'Ran pnpm typecheck' below it. A's cost is that in the default Statuses list two rows are bright, the running one and the failed 'Ran pnpm migrate --env staging', so the error is a little less unique. The red icon and the error panel still set it apart. Everything else is pixel-identical in both: the error, long-content, collapsed 'Worked for 50s, 4 steps' and expanded panel stories. Both have the same small flaw: in the error story, the bottom of the open error panel touches the next row with no gap.

Only the running row's label differs between the two. The error and long-content shots are byte-identical, and everything else matches pixel for pixel. In A, 'Running pnpm test' (default and mobile-420) and 'Running pnpm test billing' (group-1280 and group-420) are bright white, like the failed row, so the live step reads first in each list. In B the running label is the same muted grey as finished 'Ran …' rows, and only the small sky spinner sets it apart, so in the group 'Running' section it nearly blends in with 'Read src/billing/charge.ts' above it. The streaming story shows the gap most: B's only row, 'Running pnpm test', is dimmer than its own output block, so the header looks settled while output is still arriving. B's calmer list has one benefit: the red-x failed row is the only bright label. But muting a step that is still in progress costs more clarity than that restraint gains. Density, copy, borders, radius, the error-tone panel, long-content wrapping and scrolling, and the 420px layouts are otherwise equal.
